note: All 30 why lines read against their study. Re-read today: Ruby, Dunn and colleagues 2011 (full paper). Williams 2008 couldn't be reached (the paper page asks for a human check). The rest were checked in the Move review (19 Nov).

cards.note: The gym members only imagined starting with their favourite exercise; they didn't do it. Say: "Gym-goers who pictured starting with their favourite exercise expected to enjoy it more."

"In four studies" is too many: two of the four showed workouts were more enjoyable than predicted; the other two changed how people thought ahead. Say "In two studies, gym-goers enjoyed workouts more than they'd predicted."

Williams and colleagues 2008: only the title could be read ("Acute affective response to a moderate-intensity exercise stimulus predicts physical activity participation 6 and 12 months later"). It matches the why line, but the participants (new exercisers?) still aren't confirmed. Flagged in the Move review too.
Men only, and about muscle (flagged in the Move review; the pretend people stumbled on it too). A study of men and women getting back into exercise would fit "I keep starting and stopping" better.
Noetel 2024 studied people with depression; "ease low mood" is fair. Flagged and kept in the Move review.
